post.caption: Flawless means no flaws at 10x. The Gemological Institute of America's clarity scale has 11 grades. Features inside a diamond are called inclusions, and blemishes are only on the surface, such as scratches or nicks. Flawless means neither is visible under 10x magnification. The institute introduced its 10x loupe in 1934, the final grade is always set under that loupe, and the institute built its grading system in the early 1950s. Graders weigh how big each feature is and where it sits. Flawless is rare, because few diamonds are free of inclusions, and most slightly included diamonds show no inclusions visible to the naked eye.
